html_en:
A day of infrastructure maturity and honest reckoning: as AI agents move from demos into production, the hard questions — about quality, collaboration, and what we're giving up — are finally getting serious answers.

🔧 Anthropic Owns Its Mistakes — And Rebuilds the Plumbing

In a refreshingly candid postmortem, Anthropic detailed three separate bugs that quietly degraded Claude Code for weeks — and why they were so hard to catch. The culprits: a reasoning effort downgrade meant to reduce latency, a caching bug that made Claude seem "forgetful and repetitive," and an overzealous verbosity-reduction prompt that hurt coding quality. Each hit a different slice of traffic on a different schedule, making the aggregate look like mysterious, inconsistent degradation.

The fixes are live. As a gesture of good faith, Anthropic reset usage limits for all subscribers as of April 23rd. The episode is a useful case study in how production AI systems fail in non-obvious ways — and why user feedback, however anecdotal it seems, often catches what evals miss.

Alongside the postmortem, Anthropic published a deep architectural post on Managed Agents, explaining how they decoupled the agent "brain" (Claude + harness) from the "hands" (sandboxes) and the session log. The core insight borrows from OS design: stable abstractions outlast any particular implementation.

Building Managed Agents meant solving an old problem in computing: how to design a system for "programs as yet unthought of." Decades ago, operating systems solved this problem by virtualizing hardware into abstractions — process, file — general enough for programs that didn't exist yet.

The practical result: self-hosted sandboxes and MCP tunnels are now available, letting enterprise customers keep agent execution — files, databases, private APIs — entirely within their own perimeter. Partners including Cloudflare, Daytona, Modal, and Vercel are listed as supported sandbox providers.

⚡ Claude Code Gets a Self-Care Routine

Boris Cherny's announcement of /checkup was the day's most-shared Claude Code update — 6,600+ likes and counting. The new command audits your local setup: cleaning unused MCPs, deduplicating CLAUDE.md files, enabling auto mode, and pre-approving frequently denied read-only commands.

New in Claude Code: /checkup
Run /checkup to:
1. Clean up unused skills/MCPs/plugins and save context
2. Dedup your local CLAUDE.md against the checked in CLAUDE.md
3. Break up root CLAUDE.md into nested CLAUDE.md's + skills
4. Turn off slow hooks...
/checkup confirms with you before making any changes. Enjoy!
— @bcherny

Meanwhile, @_catwu previewed Claude Tag, a multiplayer evolution of Claude Code that moves beyond individual agentic sessions toward team-level AI coordination — monitoring channels, doing proactive work, and retaining memory across conversations. "AI used to finish your sentence. Then, it wrote entire features. Now, Claude Tag can monitor your channels, do proactive work for you, the whole team can steer it, and it remembers what you told it last week."

🤖 Grok 4.5 Makes Its Rounds

xAI's Grok 4.5 is quietly becoming the model du jour for developer integrations. Guillermo Rauch announced it's available to all Vercel customers; @ryolu_ confirmed it's live in Cursor. Box CEO Aaron Levie offered a useful frame:

As models get much better at coding, math, reasoning, and are trained on a variety of key verticals, we're going to see more leaps in what you can do with enterprise data and documents. — @levie

Over at OpenAI, late-night sushi orders at the office signal something is imminent. @thsottiaux: "We were resetting last week. This week we are SHIPPING." A livestream at 10am was teased — details pending.

🧠 The Collaboration Problem Nobody Wants to Talk About

One of the more thought-provoking observations of the day came from Zara Zhang, who surfaced an uncomfortable side effect of maximal AI adoption:

Talked to a super agent-pilled founder. He bought Codex Max for all team members, and everybody pretty much gets all work done thru talking to their Codex all day. The side effect: people stopped talking to each other. Meetings are cancelled, collaboration is minimal, and team culture got worse. So much of enterprise AI usage is single-player now. — @zarazhangrui

Her proposed frame — moving from human-agent collaboration to human-human-agent collaboration — is worth sitting with. Claude Tag, mentioned above, is one answer. But the cultural question is harder than the technical one.

Amjad Masad pushed back on the benchmark obsession from a different angle: "When do we stop comparing autonomous agents to hand-written code? You don't see compilers comparing to engineers hand-writing assembly." The framing shift he's calling for — agents as infrastructure, not as junior engineers — is overdue.

✍️ Keeping Your Voice in the Age of the Slot Machine

The latest episode of Every's AI & I with writer Greg (Watch/Listen: How a Writer Uses AI Without Losing His Voice) is a quiet counterweight to the shipping frenzy. Greg's approach to protecting creative attention is almost monastic: a separate laptop that blocks the internet, no phone until after lunch, deliberate barriers between deep work and the dopamine loop of AI tools.

"As soon as I touch my phone, I feel the chemical shift and I can't go into any kind of deep thinking place or deep attention place or deep focus place." — Greg, AI & I

Host Dan Shipper put the tension cleanly: "There's something about working with AI that feels very dopamine driven... you can use it to do incredible work and also it's sort of a slot machine." Greg's answer isn't abstinence — he's vibe-coding his own Quicken replacement and newsletter software (saving, by his account, $67,000 a year on Campaign Monitor) — but rather intentionality about which parts of himself he's willing to let the machine touch.

It's a distinction that @swyx gestured at in praising Theo's hand-drawn Excalidraw slides over "claudeslopped thin color border 'professional' looking" decks: "humanity, thoughtfulness, parsimonious concision over badly rewarded verbosity." In a world saturating with polished AI output, rawness is becoming the signal.
html_zh:
今天的AI圈有一个清晰的主旋律：工具正在成熟，但代价与边界也在浮现——从Anthropic坦承的质量退步，到企业智能体协作的文化代价，再到开发者们对"人味"与"AI味"之间那条越来越模糊的边界线的焦虑。

🔧 Anthropic的自我解剖：Claude Code经历了什么

上个月，不少Claude Code用户反映模型质量"变笨了"。Anthropic罕见地发布了一篇详细的事后复盘，将问题归因于三个独立改动的叠加效应——而非模型本身的退步。

事情的经过是这样的：首先，3月4日，团队将Claude Code的默认推理强度从「高」调为「中」，以解决部分用户遇到的界面卡顿问题。接着，3月26日，一个本该优化缓存效率的改动引入了Bug，导致Claude在每轮对话中都会遗忘此前的推理过程，而不是仅在会话闲置一小时后才清除。最后，4月16日，一条旨在减少啰嗦的系统提示词与其他改动叠加，反而损害了代码质量。三个问题发生在不同时间、影响不同流量切片，外部看起来就像"广泛、无规律的能力下降"。

「这不是用户应该期待的Claude Code体验。截至4月23日，我们已重置所有订阅用户的使用限额。」
—— Anthropic工程博客

值得注意的是，Anthropic在这篇文章里承认：他们的内部评测和使用数据，在早期并没有复现出用户反映的问题。这是一个关于AI产品质量监控局限性的重要警示。

与此同时，Anthropic也发布了Managed Agents架构解析与自托管沙箱及MCP隧道等企业级功能更新——将"大脑"（Claude与调度逻辑）与"双手"（执行环境）解耦，允许企业将敏感数据和工具执行保留在自己的安全边界内。

🚀 Claude Code的新动作与多人协作的野心

就在Anthropic修复"旧伤"的同时，产品层面的动作毫不停歇。Boris Cherny 宣布了Claude Code的新命令 /checkup，一口气解决了七个令开发者头疼的问题——从清理无用的MCP插件、去重CLAUDE.md文件，到把根目录的配置拆解成嵌套结构，再到预先批准常用的只读命令。

「新功能：/checkup。运行它可以：清理未使用的skills/MCPs/plugins以节省上下文；去重你的本地CLAUDE.md；将根目录CLAUDE.md拆分成嵌套结构；关闭慢速hooks；更新到最新版本……/checkup会在做任何更改前与你确认。」
—— @bcherny

更有野心的是多人协作方向。Cat Wu 宣布将举办一场直播，展示如何从单人Claude Code进化到多人协作的「Claude Tag」：

「AI曾经帮你补全句子，然后能写完整个功能。现在，Claude Tag可以监控你的频道、主动为你和整个团队工作，还记得你上周跟它说过什么。」
—— @_catwu

⚡ Grok 4.5登场，模型军备竞赛继续

xAI的Grok 4.5本周悄然完成了一轮渠道铺货。Guillermo Rauch 宣布其已向所有Vercel用户开放，@ryolu_ 则表示其已登陆Cursor。Box CEO Aaron Levie 对新模型在企业场景的潜力表示认可：

「最新的AI模型在处理复杂知识工作者任务方面变得非常出色，尤其是法律、专业服务、医疗等垂直领域。Grok 4.5在成本与性能上又是一个不错的入口。」
—— @levie

与此同时，OpenAI方面也显露出发布前的紧张气氛。工程师 @thsottiaux 在深夜发帖，以办公室门口堆满的外卖为证，暗示新东西即将到来：

「上周我们在复盘。这周我们要发货。请关注上午10点的直播。」
—— @thsottiaux

🧠 AI让团队沉默了——这是进步还是代价？

本周最值得深思的观察来自 @zarazhangrui，她记录了一个正在发生的组织实验：

「我和一位极度相信智能体的创始人聊过。他给所有团队成员买了Codex Max，大家整天靠和Codex对话完成工作。副作用是：人们不再互相交流了。会议取消，协作减少，团队文化变差了……我们需要超越人-人协作，也超越人-智能体协作，走向人-人-智能体协作。」
—— @zarazhangrui

这个观察与本周一档播客形成了有趣的呼应。Watch/Listen: How a Writer Uses AI Without Losing His Voice — AI & I by Every。节目中，作家Greg分享了他如何在使用AI的同时保护自己最珍贵的东西——那个能写出"奇怪的书"的自我：

「我有一台专门用来写作的笔记本电脑，上面屏蔽了一切。如果我不设这些障碍，我就会失去与自己另一部分的连接。那才是我最有价值的部分。没有多少人会去思考或写那些我想写的奇怪的书。作为一个人，那才是值得我投入精力的地方。」

主播 Dan Shipper 也精准地点出了这种张力：「使用AI感觉非常像多巴胺驱动……你可以用它做出令人难以置信的工作，但它也像一台老虎机。」

✍️ 反"AI味"的审美政治

最后，今天有几条关于"人味"的讨论值得一并放在这里。Shawn Wang 注意到一个细节——在一片充斥着「Claude美化」风格幻灯片的大会上，有位演讲者选择了手绘风格：

「在一个满是Claudeslopped细边框'专业'幻灯片的世界里，他选择了Excalidraw/tldraw的手绘风格，立刻传递出人情味、深思熟虑，以及对简洁的偏好——而非被糟糕地奖励的啰嗦。」
—— @swyx

@nikunj 则直接宣判：

「'精致'正在以你难以想象的速度与'slop'画上等号……我们将看到一场向原生与人性化的重大回摆。」
—— @nikunj

当AI让每个人都能产出"看起来很专业"的内容，真正的稀缺品反而变成了那些看起来像人做的东西。这大概是2025年AI美学最微妙的悖论。
